title: Displacement and velocity in a line
keyIdea: Displacement is how far you end up from the start in a chosen direction; average velocity is displacement ÷ time.

kid: Pick a direction to be positive, like east. Walking east is plus, walking west is minus.
Walk 30 m east, then 10 m west. You walked 40 m in all. But you are only 20 m east of the start. That 20 m is your displacement.
adult: Distance and speed ignore direction. Displacement and velocity are signed: choose a positive direction and give each move a sign.

Average speed = total distance ÷ time. Average velocity = displacement ÷ time. For 30 m east then 10 m west in 20 s, the average speed is 40 ÷ 20 = 2 m/s. The average velocity is 20 ÷ 20 = 1 m/s east.

familyTip: Walk along a hallway, forward then back. Measure both the steps you took and how far you ended from the start.

practice.prompt: Walk {a} m east, then {b} m west. What is the displacement east, in m?
Walk {a} m east, then {b} m west. What is the distance, in m?
One full lap of a 400 m track. Displacement?
practice.explain: You end where you started, so 0 m.

A velocity of −3 m/s (east positive) means…
pool.explain: Negative means the other way: west.

pool.prompt: Can average velocity be 0 when speed is not?
choices: Yes, if you return to the start
pool.explain: Back to the start means zero displacement.
